newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-World confection market seen doubling by 2020.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-World confection market seen doubling by 2020.

text.p: World demand for confectionery products is expected to double by the year 2020, the chief executive of the Confectionery Manufacturers of Australasia, Stuart Spencer, said on Monday.
"Most of this growth is associated with increasing affluence in nearby Asian countries," Spencer told an Australian Cane Farmers Association conference.
Asian markets are currently experiencing annual growth of about six percent in confectionery demand, Spencer said.
"The next big area (for Australia) is Asia," he said.
"For suppliers of agricultural inputs this is promising news," Spencer said. He gave no specific figures.

Currently the Australian confectionery industry is both stagnant and mature, with annual sales of about A$2 billion, but exports had been increasing at about 30 percent annually for the past five years, Spencer said. Primary export markets are Japan, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore.
Spencer said he did not expect sugar-free additives to be used as a replacement for sugar in the confectionery industry.
Texture and bulk characteristics of confectionery could only be achieved through the use of sugar, Spencer said.
